title: Narrow skill versus general intelligence claims

sections.skill: Tell narrow task performance from general intelligence claims

questions.domain: Society: history and claims about the future
questions.prompt: What is a narrow system?

choices.text: A system that can do every task that any human can do, at least as well as any human
One that does one task or a small set very well

questions.correct_answer: One that does one task or a small set very well
questions.intro: A NARROW system does one task or a small set of tasks very well: Deep Blue played chess; AlphaGo played Go; an image classifier labels photos. GENERAL INTELLIGENCE, often called AGI (artificial general intelligence), would mean flexible ability across a wide range of tasks, including new ones, at or beyond human level; definitions vary and are debated. Strong performance on one task, or even many tests, does not by itself show general intelligence. Today's chat models handle many tasks, which makes the line blurrier, but they also fail in ways people do not expect.

sections.skill: Compare narrow and general ability with a calculator and a student

questions.domain: Society: history and claims about the future
questions.prompt: The calculator is like which kind of system?

choices.text: General, because a calculator can multiply better than any person in the whole world

questions.intro: A CALCULATOR multiplies huge numbers instantly, far better than any student. But it cannot read a story, learn a new game, or decide what problem to solve. A STUDENT is slower at multiplication but flexible: they can learn new subjects and handle new situations. Being superhuman at one task, like the calculator, is different from being flexible across many, like the student.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.domain: Society: history and claims about the future
questions.prompt: A company claims its product "reached AGI." What should you ask first?

choices.text: "Can I buy it today at the lowest possible price, before everyone else hears about it?"

questions.intro: Claims about general intelligence deserve careful reading. Ask: How is "general" defined here? Which tasks were tested, and were they new to the system? How does it fail? Who is making the claim, and do they benefit from it? Experts disagree about how close current systems are to general intelligence and whether the concept is even well defined. This course does not settle that debate.
